permit_name: as now: short-term ikamet via real estate (YUKK 6458 art. 31/1-j); alternative — digital nomad certificate and visa → short-term ikamet

social_note: a pension for a self-employed marketer is not mandatory (§ 2 SGB VI — separate groups; secondary source); with KSK — 9.3 % pension, but health ≈ $8,246
feasibility_why: The title is real, but insurance ≈ $16k/year from the first year and marketing is most likely a Gewerbe (business plan, IHK).

permit_name: Digital Nomad Programme of the Ministry of Industry and Trade (CzechInvest): long-term visa for the purpose "other" (employee of a foreign company) or for business (freelancer with a Czech trade licence); IT and marketing specialists from 12 listed countries
permit_norm: Digital Nomad Programme (CzechInvest, Ministry of Industry and Trade); long-term visa under Act No. 326/1999 Coll. on the Residence of Foreign Nationals (§ 30, supporting documents § 31)
first_term: Long-term visa up to 1 year, extendable by up to 1 year (MZV); the programme application is processed within 45 days (MZV Chicago)
remote_work_norm: Employee route: the person stays employed by the foreign company and does not enter into an employment relationship in the Czech Republic; freelancer route: a Czech trade licence is required; applications are assessed by the ministry and "there is no legal entitlement to participation in the Program" (CzechInvest, MZV Chicago)
health_basis: the medical part is included in the flat sum, but a third-country OSVČ is not accepted into VZP without permanent residence (the expat-health-insurance dataset) — adult private policy
social_note: Tax and contribution terms of the Digital Nomad Programme are not stated on the official pages: not established.
cost_note: Total not computed: the official pages state no tax or contribution terms for the programme. Insurance 4,249 USD/year is the adult private policy from the expat-health-insurance dataset. The flat-tax figures of the trade-licence route are in the own_business row.
feasibility_why: The programme is open only to IT and marketing specialists from 12 listed countries and approval is discretionary; the official pages state no income threshold, insurance or tax terms (Fragomen cites an income of at least 1.5 times the average gross annual salary, not confirmed on an official page).

permit_name: Long-term visa, then long-term residence permit, for the purpose of business (Czech trade licence, živnostenské oprávnění)
permit_norm: Act No. 326/1999 Coll. on the Residence of Foreign Nationals (long-term visa § 30, supporting documents § 31; MZV); long-term residence permit for business (Ministry of the Interior)
first_term: Visa up to 1 year (MZV); long-term residence permit: initial term up to 2 years, extensions of up to 2 years (Ministry of the Interior)
remote_work_norm: A third-country national needs a trade licence: it is notified to the trade licensing office and the residence permit is presented within six months of the preliminary extract (Brno city hall); the official pages do not say whether clients must be Czech or foreign.
tax_regime: paušální daň OSVČ (income tax + pension + health insurance in one monthly payment) for self-employed with revenue up to CZK 2 million; 2026 payments CZK 9,984 / 16,745 / 27,139 per month for bands I / II / III (Financial Administration)
tax_calc: 71,395 × 24.36 ≈ 1,739,200 Kč → bracket II (16,745 Kč/month) at a 60 % norm, otherwise III (27,139 Kč/month = 325,668 Kč/year ≈ €13,369); III taken
health_basis: the medical part is included in the flat sum, but a third-country OSVČ is not accepted into VZP without permanent residence (the expat-health-insurance dataset) — adult private policy
social_note: pension and healthcare are already inside the lump-sum payment ("tax" column)
cost_note: tax 14,980 + insurance 4,249 + social contributions 0 = 19,229 $/year. Band III is taken because the sample revenue is about CZK 1.7 million; the revenue limits of the bands were not found on the official pages opened (they give the monthly payments only), the band choice follows e15.cz.
feasibility_why: The route is open to third-country nationals with a Czech trade licence (the official pages list no nationalities); they state no minimum income, only proof of funds and health insurance. Whether foreign-only clients satisfy the trade-licence route is not addressed on the official pages.
